度上修 2H26 營收與獲利預估。展望 2027 年，預估四大 CSP AI 
資本支出再成長 37% YoY，投資動能延續；惟自由現金流轉負後，
後續資本支出將更仰賴外部融資，預期對整機成本與零組件價格控
管將轉趨嚴格。同時，隨上游原物料新增產能於 2H27 至 1H28 陸
續開出，供需緊張逐步緩解，2027 年 CCL 漲價動能亦將趨緩。不
過隨著通用型伺服器材料升級、ASIC 專案陸續發酵以及低軌衛星
開始貢獻，聯茂 M6 以上營收占比將自 2026 年約 30% 提升至 
2027 年 40%，2028年有望進一步提升至50%，產品組合再升級。
此外，AI 高階應用須同時具備客戶認證與量產規模，聯茂 M9 已
通過美系 GPU 客戶認證、M10 同步送樣，產能亦大幅開出，有利

動能趨緩，因此本益比由 25 倍調降至 20 倍。不過獲利大幅上
修，目標價仍由 550 元上調至 780 元 （採用 2027 年 PER 20X 
評價；前次目標價 550 元 / 2027 年 PER 25X 評價），維持買進
評等。

items.story:
We focus on Advantech's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for its share price.
Details:
1. August sales were NT$10,419mn (-8% MoM/+88% YoY),
2. QTD revenue reached 77% of MSe, at NT$28,185mn (+8% QoQ/+59% YoY),
and 76% of consensus, at NT$28,371mn (+9% QoQ/+60% YoY).
3. By region, N.A (+106%) outperformed, while other markets, including Europe
(+52%), China (+67%), Taiwan (+96%), Japan (+73%), Korea (+79%) and
emerging markets (+75%), also performed strongly.
4. By segment, Intelligent Systems was +93% YoY, IoT Automation was +36%
YoY, while Intelligent Service grew single-digit% YoY. The Embedded Sector
grew 61% YoY, of which Embedded IoT grew 83% YoY, while Applied
Computing grew 37% YoY.
Our view:
1. We think its 3Q26 revenue is tracking ahead of market expectations and
more likely to approach 20-25% QoQ growth.
2. Management attributed the strength in August to demand from sectors
including semi, AI datacenter, energy infrastructure, and factory automation.
3. B/B ratio in August was stronger than that in July, continuing to point to a
strong revenue outlook in the coming quarters.
4. We remain constructive on Advantech, as it is well positioned to benefit
from accelerating IoT market growth amid edge AI proliferation.

items.story:
We raise our 3Q26 earnings estimates for Wiwynn by 10% on stronger-than-
expected general server momentum, while trimming 4Q26 modestly to reflect a
likely general server normalization and a slower VR200 M/P schedule.
Importantly, this does not change our core view: the inference-driven server
upcycle remains intact, with demand still running ahead of supply. The key offset
is AWS T3, which we see ramping cleanly and becoming the primary driver of 4Q
sequential growth (JPMe +6% QoQ) even if general servers cool. We now expect
AWS T3 to ramp meaningfully in 4Q and represent 50%+ of Wiwynn’s revenue
(potentially ~60% in our model). With Vera Rubin and AMD ramps also building,
Wiwynn’s AI mix could approach ~70% in 2027. We raise our 2027E/28E earnings
by 5%/2% and maintain OW with a Jun-27 PT of NT$2520 (based on 15x12-month
forward EPS). The stock has underperformed the TAIEX by 15% since September
on supply-chain noise and dilution concerns. Key upside risk is TPU v9 design
wins; key downside risk is component constraints.

constructive on medium- to long-term demand trends. Near term, we trim our 2026
EPS estimate by 5% to reflect the AWS T3 transition in 4Q26 and margin
headwinds from rising memory costs. Looking ahead, we raise our 2027/2028 EPS
forecasts by 1%/3% to reflect the dual upside drivers from liquid-cooled AWS T3
modules and 1.6T switches. Accton stock has underperformed the TWSE by ~22%
over the past three months on margin dilution concerns and AWS supply-chain
noise. We believe these fears are overdone and expect market sentiment to turn
more constructive as consignment adoption becomes better understood. With a
54% EPS CAGR over 2026–28E, we recommend investors accumulate on the
recent weakness. Stay OW with a Jun-27 PT of NT$3,700, based on 25x 12M fwd
EPS.

We raise our 3Q26/4Q26 revenue forecasts for Wistron by 14%/17% to reflect
upside to NVL72 rack shipments. Resilient GB300 demand should support a
smooth transition into VR200 starting 4Q26 and through 2027. We also believe
Wistron has secured new customers and renewed contracts on more favorable
terms as ODM capacity tightens, which should support a gradual margin uplift over
time. As a result, we raise our 2027/2028 revenue estimates by 13%/11% and
model 34%/27% EPS growth in 2027/28. We had upgraded the stock in August
on a stronger AI accelerator outlook, new AI customer wins, and Wiwynn’s
strength. We maintain OW with a Jun-27 PT of NT$260, based on 10x 12-month
forward EPS (in line with mid-cycle valuations). Wistron has underperformed the
TWSE by 41% YTD. While we understand investor concerns around working
capital pressures, we believe improved business terms and customer
diversification can address this over time. At ~8x forward P/E, the stock looks
compelling versus our 47% EPS CAGR over 2026–28. Wistron is our top pick in
the ODM space.

mix with stronger server QD revenue contribution; 2) QD TAM expansion into
higher-spec rack manifold QDs with continued share gains/new customer wins
from VR200 in 2H26; and 3) VR Ultra (VRU) spec upgrade where ZQD adoption
at ~2x ASP lifts QD content per VRU NVL72 rack ~100%. We believe market
conviction should increase on structural QD spec upgrades, share gains, and
another GM beat. With this note, we transfer coverage of Fositek to Megan Hsueh.

growth could reach 42% Q/Q, with backlog supporting 4Q growth.
2.Backlog supports 4Q growth, while investor feedback flags near-term margin
concerns from higher depreciation and MEMS mix, with GM at 38–40% in 2H26.

+233% Y/Y, higher than MSe of NT$1,600mn, mainly driven by continual ramp of
socket capacity with probe card revenue remaining stable during the month. We see
this mainly driven by continual ramp in AI GPU, ASICs and CPU products.

revenue suggests +42% Q/Q, higher than original guidance of +35% Q/Q and MSe/
Street of +37%/28% Q/Q. As there are still many backlogs to fulfill, 4Q revenue is
likely to continue growing sequentially. However, with rising MEMS exposure, GM is
likely 38–40% in 3Q and 4Q. Current valuation is trading at 33x 2027e EPS vs. 25-
28e EPS CAGR of 111%. Recent investor feedback suggests concerns on the near-
term margin trend; benefits from new socket capacity ramp would be more than
offset by increased depreciation and more MEMS probe card revenue.

MediaTek (MTK)’s share price recorded a record-level rally in 2Q26, and a new high in 3Q26 (up
211% vs. TAIEX up 40% in Apr-May), but started seeing a correction into Oct-2026 (down 15% vs.
TAIEX down 2% MTD). The correction was due to surging market concerns, particularly over its
EMIB-T project (TPU v.9) yield and potential tape-out delay for v.9 chip. The share price dynamics
from April appear to echo the way we expected it to materialize: we argued in our March 2026
report that the next two quarters (2Q-3Q26) are the best period for MTK to perform before we need
to be concerned about TPU v.9 chip execution into 4Q26 (refer to “After 2000 days.. ”). In this report,
we fine-tune our 2026-28 EPS by -2-6%, with unchanged Buy rating and TP of TWD5,800, still
based on 25x 2027-28 average EPS (25x P/E is at the high end of its historical range; currently
trading at 18x). While some Street concerns are reasonable, particularly those over EMIB-T yield,

GUC shares have rallied ~100% since late July (vs the TAIEX up 11%), driven by a strong
wave of consensus earnings upward revisions. This is largely in line with our
observations highlighted in our 2 Aug report that “consensus expectations were way too low.”
We believe the Street is starting to acknowledge that there is a strong pipeline of CSP projects
over the next 2-3 years, including Google CPU (GOOGL US, Not rated; revenue sharply
higher in 2026 with momentum potentially sustaining into 2027F and 2028F as Axion 3
doubles silicon content from Axion 2), as well as the other top three US hyperscalers’ ASIC
and CPU projects along with Tesla’s (TSLA US, Not rated) AI5/AI6.5. GUC not only has
secured projects from top US hyperscalers, but at the same time acquired additional
meaningful customers with volume globally, e.g. China auto ASIC and US AI ASIC using a
SoW approach. However, among all, the one that has caught our attention the most is the
Google TPU v.10 compute die opportunity (though we believe the turnkey deal is yet to be
finalized) — not only because the addressable size could be significant, but this business
opportunity might originate from GUC’s G-link 3D die-on-die IP. We raise our
2026-28F EPS for GUC by 15%-37% to incorporate business upside from non-Axion projects,
and raise TP to TWD9,600 (from TWD5,800), based on an unchanged 40x target P/E, while
rolling forward valuation to the 2027-28F average EPS. We are yet to incorporate overseas
convertible bonds (ECB) in our model/EPS estimates.
